title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LA1RF_1LD0LE_1RE0RA_1LC0RD_0RE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LA1RF_1LD0LE_1RE0RA_1LC0RD_0RE---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of blocks (10)^n cut by single 1s, after a reservoir of the word 1010101 at the left end. In a drain each round trip moves one pair of the last block into the reservoir; when it is down to one pair a rebuild starts, in which a reflector Q walks left and triples the part of the list it passes. Every separator and every reservoir word is a mover, and Lean proves that the head crosses any run of movers unchanged, so every bounce is a lemma except the few cells where the head turns. On these lemmas an exact simulator runs 1.5×1018 steps without a halt. Every halt would be the head in D, moving right, on 1 0 1 1, inside one of those collisions, and nothing yet shows that no collision ever does that.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 66,332 cells have been visited and 32,786 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: linear/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 1.01). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.462).

claims.title: Crossing pairs
claims.text: D> (01)^n → (10)^n D>, E> (10)^n → (01)^n E>, (01)^n E> 0 → E> 0 (01)^n, (10)^n C> 1 → C> 1 (10)^n, for every n.

claims.title: Frozen levels and a steady drain
claims.text: At the left-end records at steps 838,623,265, 911,286,865 and 987,150,465 the tape is C> (01)^4 (1010101)^r (01)^7, then 9 segments (10)^11 11 (01)^43, then 6 segments (10)^83 11 (01)^403, then larger ones ((10)^162 11 (01)^893, (10)^565 11 (01)^893 twice, (10)^6 11 (01)^1162), and a final run (01)^m. Only r and m change: r = 5,323, 5,723, 6,123 and m = 4,323, 3,923, 3,523.

claims.title: No halt in the first 7.30×10<sup>14</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 7.30×1014 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.75×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 1,080 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: The reflector's walk
claims.text: With the head at the right end in state E and blank beyond, Q0 c a = L (01)^c 0 (01)^a E> and Q1 c a = L (01)^c 1 (01)^a E>: one bounce takes Q0 (c+1) (a+1) to Q1 c (a+3) in 4a+14 steps and Q1 (c+1) (a+1) to Q0 c (a+3) in 4a+10 steps, and k double bounces take Q0 (c+2k) (a+1) to Q0 c (a+1+4k) in 8ak+16k²+16k steps, for every c, a, k and every tape L. Q moves two cells left per bounce, the right end two cells right.

claims.title: Five drain ends in direct simulation
claims.text: Reading the tape as a list of block lengths at every left-end record, the list apart from its last block changes only at steps 2,094, 9,061, 272,814, 142,359,375 and 1,793,526,413 in the first 2.23×109 steps, each time right after the last block is down to one pair, and the next drain end is at 2,230,168,743. For example at 142,359,375 the tail 130 541 269 821 1 is followed by (11 43)^9 11 86 (83 403)^6 83 187 162 (893 565)^2 1162 6 7228, and at 1,793,526,413 1162 6 1 by 1552.

claims.title: How a rebuild goes
claims.text: Observed at every bounce of the rebuilds at 1.4×108 and 1.79×109 steps: a separator of the list (001100 in that phase) that Q passes becomes a mover 11, carried four cells right per bounce, so each block Q passes comes out as 3n (n even) or 3n−4 and 3n+4 alternately (n odd); (11 43) becomes (29 133), then (83 403). The walk ends when the first mover reaches the right end: Q is left behind as a scar 00 or 11 and a new Q starts near the right end. A later Q turns a 00 scar into a mover and stops at a 11 scar. Then the head returns to the left end and a new drain begins.

claims.title: Three more drain ends in the accelerated run
claims.text: rsim with an event hook: the drain ending at 2.23×109 is followed by a rebuild of the whole tape, reservoir included (11,198 copies of 3 become (5 13)^388 5 37 (19 35)^5209, a new reservoir starts from nothing), finished at 1.79×1012 with last block 468,864; the next drain ends at 6.48×1012 and its rebuild ends at 1.26×1014 with last block 4,737,114; that drain ends at 6.05×1014 and its rebuild was not finished at 7.3×1014. These rest on rsim's jumps (not proved); in the middle of the long rebuild, at step 107,877,479,194, rsim's tape and state equal those of a plain C simulator (822,161 cells).

claims.title: Where a halt could come from
claims.text: From the table: B is entered only from A reading 0, moving right and writing a 1, so B reading 0 sends the head back onto that 1; F is entered only as A> 0 1 x, and it halts when x = 1. A reading 0 is entered only from D reading 1 (from B it lands on the 1 just written), and D reading 1 with A then reading 0 only from E (C writes the 1 that A would read). So every halt is D> 1 0 1 1 with D moving right: a block of one pair between two extra 1s. In 3×109 steps F is entered 63,295,957 times, always on a 0, in 22 different 17-cell windows.

claims.title: Movers: the head crosses them unchanged
claims.text: At a right-end turn a mover is the word 0 0 1 1 0 followed by g pairs 01; the list's separators, the reservoir's words (g = 1) and the separators Q has passed are all movers. For any list of gaps of at least one pair, the left sweep (state E on a 0) crosses all the movers and comes out on their left in state E on a 0, and the right sweep crosses them again and comes out in state D with every mover four cells further right (after a one-pair gap it runs in state F for a while, which changes only the first cell it writes). Hence any bounce, whatever happens left of the movers, as long as the head sent in from the right in state E on a 0 comes back in state D or F without looking right, keeps the gaps between movers and shortens the last one by a pair; with Q on the left this gives Q's walk with movers in closed form.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.5×10<sup>18</sup> steps of an exact simulator
claims.text: py/mover_sim.py moves the tape a bounce at a time: k bounces at once by walk/walkm, a bounce by bounce_gen when only its left end is unusual (that end run cell by cell), and every other bounce one machine step at a time, runs of pairs crossed by the rules of lean/Rules.lean. Only its bookkeeping is unproved; its tape and state equal those of direct simulation (c/dump.c) after 203,633 bounces at step 29,361,299,373 (441,628 cells). Its tape also equals that of the accelerated simulator rsim at steps 1,008,073,404,791 and 695,788,802,905,521 (57,654,285 cells). From step 273,791 it reaches 1.57×1018 steps (1.57 billion bounces, 12 million collisions run cell by cell) without a halt; the rebuild that starts at 6.05×1014 has not finished by then. Its drain ends at 6.48×1012 and 6.05×1014 give exactly the lists of the accelerated run, for example ... 5707 563005 177397 4764477 1 with a reservoir of 5,205,978 words.

claims.title: The collisions seen so far
claims.text: A halt can only come from a collision run cell by cell: inside the mover lemmas F always reads the first cell of a gap or the 0 that starts the next mover. To 1013 steps there are 57 different collision runs, all made of a few pieces: the left sweep crossing a gap or a mover, the right sweep passing a mover (E1 D1 A0 B1 F0) or turning at one (E1 D1 A0 B0, D1 A1), and the turns at Q and at the two ends. In all of them F reads a 0.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only when F reads a 1, and that happens only as D> 1 0 1 1 (see below). Every bounce is a proved mover lemma except the cells where the head turns, so a halt would have to come from one of those collisions; none of the 57 kinds seen to 1013 steps halts, and an exact simulator finds none to 1.5×1018, but no invariant yet rules out a different collision later. CTL (windows of 2 to 5 cells) and NGramCPS (widths 2 to 8, history, LRU) fail.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: D, E and C crossing runs of pairs.
Two cells left per bounce, for every size (Lean).
In direct simulation to 2.2×10<sup>9</sup> steps, each followed by a rebuild.
No halt in the C simulator; 66,332 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.75×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: Frozen levels
html: Everything between the reservoir (1010101)^r and the last run (01)^m is identical in the samples at 8.4·108, 9.1·108 and 9.9·108 steps. Segment sizes grow from level to level (43, 403, then about 900 and more), which suggests that each level was built when the previous drain ran out.

sections.heading: Draining the last run
html:
Between samples, 400 pairs of the last run disappear (4,323, 3,923, 3,523) and 400 copies of 1010101 join the reservoir (5,323, 5,723, 6,123). The tape grows by 2,000 cells to the left. The head crosses runs of pairs in one go (proved in Lean) and carries the material across the frozen levels.

What halting would need. F reading a 1. The steady drain makes the same moves each time, so a halt could only come at a transition, such as when the last run is empty and a new level has to be built. That transition is decoded in the next section.

sections.heading: When the last run is used up
html: Read from the left, the tape is a reservoir of words 1010101 and then a list of blocks (10)^n separated by single 1s. In a drain each round trip of the head moves one pair from the last block into the reservoir. When the last block is down to one pair the head stops reaching the left end and a rebuild starts.

The head now bounces between the right end of the tape and a reflector Q, one extra cell in a background of pairs. Each bounce moves Q two cells left and the right end two cells right; Lean proves this for every size (walk in lean/Walk.lean). Every separator Q passes turns into a mover that the head carries four cells right per bounce. What Q has passed therefore moves away from it twice as fast as Q moves, and comes out stretched three times: block n becomes 3n, 3n−4 or 3n+4. So 11 43 becomes 29 133, and after a second walk 83 403.

A walk ends when the first mover catches up with the right end, which grows more slowly. Q is left behind as a scar and a new Q starts near the right end; a later Q turns a 00 scar into a mover and stops at a 11 scar. When the walks are over the head runs back to the left end and the next drain starts with a new, longer last block. These collision rules are observed, bounce by bounce, not proved.

Where a halt could come from. Following the table backwards, every halt is the head in state D, moving right, on 1 0 1 1: a block of a single pair between two extra 1s. The drains never meet it. The rebuilds are where blocks get that short, so a proof of non-halting needs exact rules for the collisions and an invariant of the lists that keeps this word out.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 1.01). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.462).
After 109 steps the tape spans 66,332 cells (10,417 left of the start, 42,071 right), with a density of 1s of 0.494.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A list of blocks (10)^n after a reservoir of the word 1010101; drains move the last block into the reservoir one pair per round trip, and each drain end starts a rebuild in which a reflector walks left and triples every block it passes. The head crosses runs of separators unchanged (proved), and an exact simulator on that runs 1.5·10^18 steps without a halt.
family: bouncer feeding a reservoir, rebuilt by a tripling reflector
